trigger.finding: The apparent 24-Newton/96-backtracking cliff was generated by a zero-correction TRIDAG test stub. A state-updating Thomas/TRIDAG control removed the cliff and exposed accepted higher-cost routes.
trigger.implication: Convergence, solver-cost and performance-tail claims require an explicit state-updating Reference linear-solver binding.

source_bound_findings.current_headcalc_primary_path: HeadCalc calls external TRIDAG for every normal tridiagonal Newton solve.
source_bound_findings.current_headcalc_fallback_path: The in-HeadCalc band solver is entered only when TRIDAG returns nonzero ierror and is counted as alternative_solver_calls.
source_bound_findings.current_swap5_materialization: No production tridag.f90 is present under src/legacy/b1_10_port on the F-SI18 postimage; isolated test linksets supply the external symbol through test fixtures.
source_bound_findings.legacy_reference_primary_solver: Official SWAP 4.3.1 source contains SWAP/tridag.f90 and compile_link_431_linux.sh explicitly compiles tridag.f90 before headcalc.f90.
source_bound_findings.legacy_reference_algorithm: TRIDAG is the state-updating tridiagonal Thomas-style solve; banded pivoting remains a rare-case fallback.
source_bound_findings.production_build_claim_boundary: This finding does not claim that a final SWAP5 production executable is currently broken. It establishes that the isolated Reference Richards seam is not yet self-contained for numerical-behavior qualification.

owner_decision_questions: Is the legacy TRIDAG algorithm part of the intended full-accuracy REFERENCE numerical contract?
Should the minimal seam materialize the exact qualified legacy TRIDAG implementation as an F-SI-owned Reference component, or place it behind an explicit Reference linear-solver interface?
Can the legacy implementation be made worker-local/reentrant without changing arithmetic or failure semantics?
How is the existing banded fallback kept explicitly fallback-only and separately diagnosed?
Which exact source provenance and independent F-VQ evidence are required before PE may use the state-updating route for tail characterization?

candidate_paths.A: Materialize a source-bound Reference TRIDAG component with preserved arithmetic/failure semantics and no new policy.
candidate_paths.B: Introduce the smallest explicit Reference linear-solver seam and bind it to a source-bound TRIDAG implementation; keep HeadCalc independent of test-provided external symbols.
candidate_paths.C: Promote the existing banded fallback to primary only if separate theory/source evidence proves that this is an intended Reference-policy change. C is not presumed valid.

hard_constraints: No zero-step or numerically inert stub may support convergence, solver-cost or performance-tail qualification.
Do not promote the band fallback to primary silently.
Do not alter nonlinear, temporal or mass tolerances to obtain acceptance.
Mass conservation and transaction semantics remain unchanged and hard.
Scratch must remain worker/job-owned; no new persistent per-column scratch.
No filesystem, calendar or hidden global-runtime dependency may be introduced into the kernel/solver contract.
No production edit before provenance and minimal-seam decision are persisted.
next_action: Audit exact TRIDAG arithmetic, dependencies, scratch and failure semantics against the current workspace/HeadCalc architecture, then choose the smallest source-bound seam before any production edit.
